The 2016 GSX-S1000 has the better and safer brake system. It features Brembo radial-mount front calipers with ABS as standard, offering superior stopping power and modulation. The Z1000 (2014/2016) uses Tokico calipers with ABS, which are competent but generally considered a step below Brembo in feel and performance. The GSX-S1000's Brembo setup is widely regarded as class-leading in that segment.

The Kawasaki Z1000 (2014–2016) uses a dual 310mm petal disc setup with radial-mount 4-piston calipers up front and a single 250mm disc with a single-piston caliper at the rear — no ABS as standard on base models (ABS version available).

The Suzuki GSX-S1000 (2016) uses dual 310mm discs with Brembo-sourced 4-piston radial-mount Monobloc calipers up front and a single 220mm disc at the rear, with ABS standard on most markets.

**The GSX-S1000 is generally considered better and safer** due to:
- **Brembo Monobloc calipers** — widely regarded as superior in feel and stopping power
- **ABS standard** — significant safety advantage
- Better overall brake feedback and modulation per contemporary reviews

The Z1000's brakes are competent but the GSX-S1000 has the edge in both hardware quality and active safety.
